messages:
amanda: seeing apiserver 502/503 spike in eu-west-3 starting ~02:10 UTC. etcd leader WAL fsync spikes and controller-manager leader flips. new gpu-nodepool scale up completed ~02:05. anyone else?

rick: I see it too. etcd leader p95 write latency jumped to 320ms around the same time. watch events backlog increasing.

priyanka: digging nodes that joined: a batch of 40 GPU nodes landed. kube-proxy reports lots of new connection churn; conntrack entries rising to 95% on a subset of NAT gateways.

amanda: output snip: 
```
# kubectl -n kube-system top pods | egrep "etcd|apiserver|controller-manager"
etcd-eu-west-3-0         2/2   Running   0   12m
apiserver-eu-west-3-1   2/2   Running   1   12m
controller-manager-0    0/1   CrashLoopBackOff  6   8m
```

priyanka: controller-manager logs: `error getting leader election record: etcdserver: request timed out` and then `I am not the leader` repeatedly. leader lease renew fails intermittently.

rick: infra metrics show NAT SNAT port pool exhaustion on the east eu-west-3 egress node group at 02:09. high ephemeral outbound flows from kubelet image pulls and a burst of healthchecks from node-exporter after join.

ops-bot: automated mitigation: cordoned nodepool gpu-spot-batch-3 and scaled down join rate to 4 nodes/minute.

amanda: good. that immediately reduced conntrack pressure and etcd p99 dropped to ~60ms after ~4 mins. apiserver 5xx count fell.

priyanka: root cause hypothesis: simultaneous node joins create two correlated issues: (1) kube-proxy / kubelet creating many outbound connections (image pulls, cloud metadata, readiness probes) exhausting SNAT ports, (2) etcd WAL fsync amplified by kube-controller-manager churn as controllers try to reconcile new nodes. Combined -> apiserver latency and leader timeouts.

amanda: agreed. short-term fixes: 1) stagger node joins (already doing), 2) pre-warm NAT by increasing SNAT pool size for gpu nodepools, 3) throttle kubelet readiness probe frequency for onboarding nodes, 4) add backpressure on autoscaler for mass scale-ups.

rick: also opened RH-OPS-9123 for a kernel tuning tweak on WAL sync coalescing for etcd hosts; will double-check disk sched and nvme queue settings on controlplane.

priyanka: cost note: pre-warming NAT and reserving larger ephemeral IP pools will increase egress infra spend ~4-6% in the short term for eu-west-3. flagged CFO FYI.

amanda: long-term: enhance the autoscaler to use a "graceful onramp" mode for large GPU pool growth, plus a post-join job that batches noncritical image pulls via a local cache. Also consider moving heavy image-pulling workloads to a staging registry in-region to reduce cross-regional egress.

bench-bot: perf data attached: sample period 02:05-02:15 UTC, etcd wal_io_time_mean 18ms -> 190ms at peak, conntrack_count 120k -> 560k on affected NAT.

rick: action owners: RH-OPS-9123 (kernel/etcd tuning) assigned to me, RH-AUTO-2211 (autoscaler onramp) to priyanka, RH-NAT-3345 (SNAT capacity bump) to infra-net.

amanda: schedule a post-incident sync + RCA doc. we should mark this P1 for control plane reliability and include Dedicated customer impact note.

priyanka: I'll draft the RCA and include steps for runbook updates (add pre-warm check and scale-up gate).

amanda: thanks all. leaving thread open for RCA link and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
